function: DDPG learns RIS phase shifts to maximize VU offloading rate; modified MADDPG learns VU offloading and local-execution power to minimize power and buffer length in RIS-aided VEC (p. 5-7).
system: BS with M antennas (M not given), K=8 single-antenna vehicles, reflecting RIS with N=36 elements and 3-bit phases, direct plus RIS links, OFDM; band not stated (p. 4-5, 9).
method: Reinforcement learning: centralized DDPG for RIS phase shifts, modified MADDPG (twin global critic plus local critics) for VU powers; trained in simulation, 1000 episodes (p. 5-9).
data_channel: Simulated in Python: distance-based path loss with exponentially distributed small-scale fading (direct links), Rician pure-LoS (RIS links); Poisson task arrivals; no 3GPP model or dataset (p. 4, 9).
test_conditions: Same urban-road setting for training and testing (K=8, N=36); tests average 10 rounds of 50 slots over task arrival rates 1-4 Mbps; Table I lists 3 Mbps (p. 8-10).
baselines: Learned: centralized DDPG and TD3; NO-RIS (no RIS) and Random-RIS (random phase shifts); compared on power consumption and buffer length (p. 9-10).
metrics: Total and per-VU power consumption, buffer length, reward convergence (p. 9-11).
complexity: Order of training complexity, e.g. modified MADDPG O(K(E*S-I)(GA+GC+2UA+2UC)) + O((E*S-I)(2GC+4UC)); DDPG and TD3 orders given; no runtime (p. 8-9).
q1_support: p. 4: "power component, which is assumed to be exponentially" distributed - custom path loss with exponential small-scale fading (direct links) and Rician pure-LoS (RIS links) in the authors' simulator; no 3GPP model, public dataset or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 8: "model, where each round contains 50 test slots, and each result" - tests reuse the training environment; Table I (p. 9) gives one setting (K = 8, N = 36, eta = 3 Mbps) and Fig. 3 trains a separate DDPG per N; no unseen scenario, band or dataset is stated.
q3_support: p. 9: "compare it with the traditional centralized DDPG and TD3" - standard learned baselines on the same problem, compared on power consumption and buffer length (Figs. 6-9); p. 10: "RIS assistance and with random RIS phase-shift have their" - non-learned NO-RIS and Random-RIS baselines (Fig. 6).
q4_support: p. 9: "O(K · (E · S − I)(GA + GC + 2UA + 2UC ))" - order of complexity of the modified MADDPG local agents, plus a global-critic term.
q5_support: p. 2: "The source code has been released at: https://github.com/qiongwu86/" DDPG-RIS-MADDPG-POWER (footnote 1).
notes: Included as area 3: the DDPG agent learns the RIS phase shifts (physical layer) and the MADDPG agents learn VU power allocation jointly in a decomposed scheme, so it is not excluded as above-PHY. Table I (p. 9) and the legends of Figs. 6-9 (p. 10) were read from page images. q2 is 0 because the paper does not state that a model trained at one setting was tested at another: Table I lists eta = 3 Mbps while Figs. 6-7 sweep 1-4 Mbps, and a load sweep is not a new scenario. q3 uses centralized DDPG and TD3 as the learned baselines and Random-RIS and NO-RIS as the non-learned ones.
